title: Final tight polish of the best packing
spec: After the basin-hopping loop ends, and only once, re-run SLSQP from the unperturbed best centres and 0.999 * best radii with options maxiter=500 and ftol=1e-13, then clip, repair and keep the result only if its radius sum is larger than the incumbent's. This recovers the small slack left by the default ftol=1e-6 stopping and by the repair shrink, without paying the tight tolerance on every hop. Reserve time for it by ending the hop loop 1.5 s earlier than now.

title: Accept equal-sum hops to drift on plateaus
spec: In the basin-hopping loop, keep a separate current packing cur, initialised to best. Each hop perturbs cur, not best. Accept the new packing as cur if its radius sum is >= cur's sum - 1e-7, so that the chain can wander across near-degenerate optima such as rattler moves. Update best only when the sum is strictly greater than best's. Every 20 hops without an improvement of best, reset cur = best.

title: Warm-start radii in hops
spec: Give _solve_once an optional argument r0=None. When it is given, use x0 = concatenate([centers0.ravel(), r0]) in place of the constant INIT_RADIUS. In the basin-hopping loop, pass r0 = 0.9 * best radii, so that SLSQP starts from the incumbent radius pattern, which is near-feasible after the perturbation, and not from equal small radii. The restart phase stays unchanged.

title: Kreisselmeier-Steinhauser aggregated overlap stage
spec: Before the exact SLSQP solve in _solve_once, run one SLSQP pass on a smooth surrogate. Replace the pairwise non-overlap constraints with a single KS aggregate per circle: g_i = -(1/rho) * log(sum_j exp(-rho * slack_ij)), where slack_ij = dist_ij - r_i - r_j and the wall slacks are included, with rho ramped from 20 to 200 over two sub-solves. Feed the output into the existing exact-constraint SLSQP as the start point. The exact stage and _repair stay unchanged, so validity is still guaranteed.

title: Smaller basin-hopping perturbation
spec: Lower HOP_SD from 0.04 to 0.025 so that each hop explores closer to the incumbent. This is about half of a typical radius (~0.09). With smaller hops, more of them should land in nearby, slightly better basins rather than in worse, distant ones. Change nothing else.

title: Final fine-hop polishing phase
spec: Split the basin-hopping phase: for the last 25% of the total budget (time from 0.75*budget to budget), use hop sd HOP_SD/4 = 0.01 in place of HOP_SD. This gives an intensification phase of tiny perturbations that tunes the contact graph around the incumbent after the broader exploration. Keep the same acceptance rule (strict improvement of best).

title: Plateau-drift acceptance in basin hopping
spec: In the basin-hopping loop, keep the current packing as a separate state from best. Accept a new local optimum into the current state whenever its radius sum is within 1e-6 of the current state's sum, even when it is slightly worse than best, so the chain can drift across degenerate optima of equal sum. Always update best when a strictly higher sum is found. The hop perturbation and the SLSQP and repair steps are unchanged. Note that this is a schedule of acceptance, not a new hop move.

title: Adaptive hop step size
spec: In basin hopping, keep a running step sd starting at HOP_SD. Multiply it by 1.15 after a hop that fails to improve the best sum and by 0.85 after a success, clipped to [0.01, 0.1]. Use this sd for the noise.

title: Concentric ring-layer starts
spec: Add a start generator that places circles on two or three concentric square rings inside the unit square, with a random number of circles per ring (summing to n), a random ring offset in [0, 0.05], and a random angular phase per ring. Add small Gaussian jitter of sd 0.01 and clip to the box, then pass the start through _relax. Roughly a third of the restart pool uses this generator; the rest stays uniform random. This targets layered packings that uniform random starts rarely reach.

title: Cheaper hop solves for more hops
spec: Give _solve_once a max_iter argument with default MAX_ITER. In the basin-hopping loop use max_iter=100. If the resulting repaired sum is within 0.002 of best's sum, run a second _solve_once from the resulting centres with max_iter=MAX_ITER and use that result. This screens bad hops cheaply and gives roughly 1.5x more hops in the same time.

title: Radius-ordered hop: perturb only small circles
spec: In basin hopping, add noise with sd 3*HOP_SD to the centres of the 8 smallest-radius circles in the best packing and sd 0.3*HOP_SD to the others, since small circles sit in loose holes whose arrangement matters most.

title: Subset re-randomisation hop
spec: In the basin-hopping loop, with probability 0.5 pick k=2..4 random circles and reposition their centres uniformly in the square, leaving the others unchanged (plus small noise sd 0.005), then run SLSQP and repair as usual. Otherwise use the existing Gaussian hop.

title: Wall bounds via SLSQP bounds
spec: Remove the four wall-constraint blocks and the r>=0 block from cons, and pass bounds to minimize: centres in [0,1], radii in [0,0.5]. Keep the pair-distance constraints, plus add wall constraints only as c-r>=0 forms if needed for validity. The repair step still guarantees validity. This shrinks the constraint count and speeds up SLSQP, giving more restarts.

title: Log-uniform multi-scale hop sizes
spec: In the basin-hopping loop, draw the noise sd per hop as exp(uniform(log 0.01, log 0.08)) instead of the fixed HOP_SD. Keep everything else the same.

title: Heavy-tailed hop noise
spec: In the basin-hopping loop, replace the Gaussian perturbation rng.normal(0, HOP_SD, c.shape) with a Student-t perturbation with 2 degrees of freedom: 0.5 * HOP_SD * rng.standard_t(2, c.shape), clipped elementwise to [-0.3, 0.3], and clip the perturbed centres to [0.02, 0.98] before the solve. Most circles then barely move while a few make large jumps, which mixes local refinement and occasional rearrangement of one or two circles in a single move type.

title: Clock-guarded budget use
spec: Check time.process_time() inside the restart pool loop and before each SLSQP solve in the hop phase, and break out as soon as the budget is reached. This removes the overshoot of a whole pool round past the 80 percent mark and uses any leftover time on one more hop. Keep the hard budget at TIME_FRACTION * time_limit so the 45 s CPU ceiling is never close. The only code change is the in-loop time checks.

title: Growing restart pool schedule
spec: Make POOL depend on the restart round index: round k uses pool size min(40, 10 * 2**(k-1)), and KEEP stays at 3. Early rounds are cheap and explore many starts, and later rounds spend more relaxations on the same budget. The round index is counted from 0 in the restart phase, and the hop phase is unchanged. Only the pool size varies across rounds.

title: Larger relax pool, fewer refined
spec: Change POOL from 20 to 40 and KEEP from 3 to 2. The cheap L-BFGS relax screens more random starts, and only the two lowest-energy ones get the expensive SLSQP refine. The restart phase therefore spends its time on better-screened starts. Change nothing else.

title: Wider relaxed pool, fewer refinements per round
spec: Change the restart-round sizing from POOL = 20, KEEP = 3 to POOL = 60, KEEP = 1. The cheap L-BFGS relaxations are a small fraction of the cost of an SLSQP solve, so this makes each SLSQP solve start from the best of 60 relaxed configurations instead of the top 3 of 20, at roughly the same number of SLSQP solves per second. Only the two constants change.

title: Replicate-free budget split tuning: HOP_START 0.2
spec: Change HOP_START from 0.4 to 0.2 so more of the 24 s budget goes to basin hopping from the best packing, which was the main gain in slot 8. No other change.

title: Replicate mirror-symmetric starts (slot 16)
spec: Re-implement the slot 16 change: in the random-restart pool, build half of the start configurations mirror-symmetric about x=0.5. Draw n//2 centres uniformly in [INIT_LOW, 0.5] x [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW], append their mirror images (1-x, y), and when n is odd add one centre on x=0.5 at a uniform y. Then relax these starts with _relax like the others. The other half stays uniform. This is meant to confirm the -2.9386 single run.

title: Squared-distance pair constraints
spec: Rewrite the pair constraint as squared centre distance minus (r_i+r_j)^2 >= 0, which is smooth at zero distance. Keep the rest. The repair step remains the same.

title: Stochastic selection among pool starts
spec: Replace the fixed top-KEEP selection in each restart round with a seeded random draw. Sample KEEP distinct starts from the pool with probability proportional to exp(-(E - E_min) / T), where E is the relaxed energy and T is set to the median energy of the pool. The best-energy start stays guaranteed in the sample. This keeps some diversity among restart starts while still favouring low-energy relaxations.

title: Smaller repair shrink
spec: Set SHRINK from 1e-9 to 2e-10, which still passes the 1e-10 overlap tolerance given the repair makes pairs exactly touching. Verify with a final exact check in solve: if any pair violates by more than 1e-10, subtract 1e-9 from all radii.

title: Perturb only a random subset of centres per hop
spec: In the basin-hopping loop of solve, do not add Gaussian noise to every centre. Draw k = rng.integers(3, 9) distinct circle indices with rng.choice(n, k, replace=False) and add rng.normal(0, 2*HOP_SD, (k, 2)) only to those centres. Clip the result to [0, 1] and then call _solve_once as before. All other circles start exactly at their best positions, so the hop is local but larger for the chosen circles.

title: Slack-guided hop on loosely held circles
spec: In the basin-hopping loop, with probability 0.5 perturb only the loosely constrained part of the best packing. Count each circle's contacts: pairs with centre distance minus radius sum below 1e-6, plus walls with gap below 1e-6. Pick the 6 circles with the fewest contacts (ties broken by smaller radius), move those with Gaussian noise of sd 0.08 and all other circles with sd 0.005, then run _solve_once as usual. Rattlers and under-constrained circles mark the regions where the packing wastes area, so the hop effort is concentrated there.

title: Trust-box bounds on hop solves
spec: During basin-hopping SLSQP solves only (not the random-restart solves), pass scipy bounds that limit each variable to a box of half-width 0.12 around the perturbed start, for both centres and radii, with radii also bounded below by 0. Keep the wall and non-overlap constraints as they are. The box acts as a local trust region that stops the solver from jumping to distant basins during a hop. Restarts keep unbounded variables.

title: Power-objective homotopy inside each hop
spec: In the basin-hopping loop, with probability 0.5 run the hop as two SLSQP stages. Stage 1 (maxiter 60) maximises sum(r ** q) with q drawn uniformly from {0.5, 2.0}, from the perturbed centres, under the same constraints: q = 0.5 favours equalised radii and q = 2 favours a few large circles. Stage 2 is the normal solve maximising sum(r), started from the centres and radii of stage 1. For q = 0.5 clamp radii with np.maximum(r, 1e-6) inside the objective to avoid nan. Implement this by giving _solve_once optional arguments for the objective exponent, the starting radii and maxiter.

title: C2 point-symmetric restart starts
spec: For half of the random restart draws, generate n/2 random centres in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2 and add their reflections through (0.5, 0.5), giving an exactly point-symmetric start. Use n-odd handling by placing the last circle at the centre. Relax the symmetric start with _relax as usual, so the pool contains both symmetric and unconstrained candidates. The SLSQP stage itself is unchanged and no symmetry is enforced after the start.

title: Linearly decaying hop size
spec: Replace the constant HOP_SD = 0.04 in the basin-hopping loop with a deterministic schedule in elapsed time: sd = 0.07 at the start of the hopping phase, decaying linearly to 0.015 at the end of the budget, computed from time.process_time() at each hop. Early hops then explore neighbouring basins with larger rearrangements and late hops refine the incumbent locally. There is no feedback from acceptance rates and no randomised scale; only the formula for sd changes.

title: Overpressure hop start
spec: In the basin-hopping loop, let _solve_once take an optional starting radius vector, and with probability 0.5 start the hop from the unperturbed best centres plus small Gaussian noise of sd 0.01, with radii set to 1.08 times the best radii, i.e. a deliberately overlapping, over-inflated state. SLSQP must then resolve the overlaps by pushing circles apart, which tends to change the contact graph in the tightest regions instead of moving every circle randomly. The other half of the hops stay as the current Gaussian hop with INIT_RADIUS radii.

title: Use more of the CPU budget
spec: Change TIME_FRACTION from 0.8 to 0.92 so that both the restart phase and the basin-hopping phase get about 15% more time. The split stays the same because HOP_START is a fraction of the budget. Each SLSQP call takes well under a second, so the final call ends near 28 s, far from the 45 s void limit. Change nothing else.

title: Two-best combo: mirror starts plus pre-solve grid nudge
spec: Combine the two unconfirmed -2.9386 changes. (a) Half of the restart pool starts are mirror-symmetric about x=0.5, as in slot 16: n//2 centres in the left half, mirrored to (1-x, y). (b) Before each SLSQP solve in both phases, as in slot 34, run 10 short steps of the cheap penalty relax (call _relax with options maxiter=10) on the start centres to remove gross overlaps. Keep everything else unchanged.

title: Basin hopping step size HOP_SD 0.02
spec: Reduce HOP_SD from 0.04 to 0.02 so hops stay closer to the incumbent basin and more hops give small improvements. No other change.

title: Use more of the time budget with a solve-duration guard
spec: Raise TIME_FRACTION from 0.8 to 0.93 so the basin-hopping phase gets about 16% more hops. To stay safe against the 45 s void limit, track the longest single _solve_once duration seen so far (measured with time.process_time) and, in both loops of solve, break out as soon as the remaining time before TIME_FRACTION * time_limit is less than 1.5 times that longest duration. HOP_START stays 0.4, so the restart phase also scales up. No other change.

title: Dilated relaxed starts
spec: After _relax returns a relaxed centre set for a start, scale its centres about (0.5, 0.5) by a random factor drawn uniformly from [1.00, 1.08], then clip to [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]. The dilation spreads the relaxed configuration toward the walls and separates near-touching pairs before SLSQP. The factor is drawn from the seeded rng, and the pool ranking still uses the relaxed energy before dilation.

title: Lazy repair on promising hop results
spec: In the basin-hopping loop, call _repair only when the raw SLSQP radius sum (before repair) is at least best sum minus 0.002. Otherwise discard the candidate without repairing it. Repair is the most expensive per-hop step, so this frees time for more hops. Candidates that pass the filter get the same repair and best-update logic as before, so every stored packing is still valid.

title: Smooth displacement-field hop
spec: In the basin-hopping loop, with probability 0.5 replace the independent per-circle Gaussian noise by a spatially smooth random displacement field, so that neighbouring circles move together. Draw 3 random wave vectors k with integer components in {-2, ..., 2} (not both zero), random phases in [0, 2 pi) and random 2D amplitude vectors from N(0, 0.03^2); the displacement of a circle at centre c is the sum over the 3 waves of amplitude * sin(2 pi k . c + phase). Add a small independent Gaussian jitter of sd 0.005, clip centres to [0.02, 0.98], then run _solve_once as usual.
